I'm working on adding rack awareness to the Kafka producer's built-in partitioner.

*   The BuiltInPartitioner constructor must accept two additional parameters after stickyBatchSize: a boolean rackAware flag and a String rack identifier. The constructor must still throw IllegalArgumentException when stickyBatchSize is 0 or less.

*   When rackAware is true and a rack identifier is provided, BuiltInPartitioner must prefer partitions whose leader broker is in the same rack as the configured rack identifier during sticky partition selection.

*   When rackAware is true but all partitions in the local rack are offline (no available leader in that rack), BuiltInPartitioner must fall back to selecting from partitions in other racks.

*   When rack-local partitions become available again after having been offline, BuiltInPartitioner must resume preferring those local-rack partitions over non-local ones.

*   When broker nodes do not carry rack information (rack is null or empty on the Node), BuiltInPartitioner must treat all partitions equally regardless of the rackAware setting, cycling through all available partitions.

*   The updatePartitionLoadStats method must accept a String[] partitionRacks parameter (inserted between partitionIds and length) that records the rack of each partition's leader.

*   When rackAware is true and rack-annotated load stats are provided, adaptive partitioning must confine partition selection to rack-local partitions only. The loadStatsInThisRackRangeEnd() method must return the end of the cumulative frequency range that covers only the rack-local partitions.

*   When rackAware is true and all rack-local partitions are offline (absent from the load stats), loadStatsInThisRackRangeEnd() must return the full range end, and adaptive partitioning must select from all available partitions.

*   The RecordAccumulator.PartitionerConfig constructor must accept two additional parameters: a boolean rackAware flag and a String rack identifier, appended after the existing partitionAvailabilityTimeoutMs parameter.

*   The RecordAccumulator.createBuiltInPartitioner method must accept boolean rackAware and String rack parameters in addition to its existing parameters, and must pass them through to the BuiltInPartitioner constructor.

## KIP-1123: Rack-Aware Partitioning for Kafka Producer

The terms you referenced (`rackAware`, `updatePartitionLoadStats`, `partitionRacks`) relate directly to work being done to make the producer-side `BuiltInPartitioner` rack-aware. This is tracked under **KIP-1123** and **KAFKA-19193**.

The core proposal is to extend the current default partitioner algorithm, namely the RecordAccumulator and BuiltInPartitioner classes: if automatic partitioning is needed (no record partition or key is specified, or partitioner.ignore.keys is set to true), and the client rack is specified and there are partition leaders in the same rack, select the next partition from those "nearby" partitions.

Regarding the existing load-statistics logic that your `updatePartitionLoadStats` reference concerns, the KIP notes that the current algorithm is followed in the other aspects, including load balancing. More specifically, the current default partitioning algorithm periodically rotates target partitions (if the partition and key are not set), also taking into account partition load statistics.

The implementation task is essentially to make the BuiltInPartitioner class aware of client and broker racks, thus affecting selected partitions, according to the KIP.

### Motivation

The motivation is cloud cost reduction across availability zones: in a typical Kafka setup in cloud, the cloud region has multiple availability zones (AZs), the cluster brokers are uniformly distributed across AZs, partition leaders are also distributed across AZs, clients (producers particularly) are also distributed across AZs, and inter-AZ network traffic is not free (true for many cloud providers), so it's desirable to reduce it.

### Rollout / Compatibility

The new behavior will be controlled by configuration. The introduced changes will be reflected in the documentation to the partitioner.class config. Migrating to the new version will have no impact on clients as the default configuration value keeps the old behavior.

## Overview

KAFKA-19193 is a Kafka improvement ticket titled "Rack-aware partitioning for Kafka Producer." It was created by Ivan Yurchenko, who is also the assignee, with the goal to make the BuiltInPartitioner class aware of client and broker racks, thus affecting selected partitions, according to KIP-1123.

## The KIP (KIP-1123)

The ticket is backed by **KIP-1123: Rack-aware partitioning for Kafka Producer**. The KIP proposes to extend the current default partitioner algorithm—the RecordAccumulator and BuiltInPartitioner classes—so that if automatic partitioning is needed (no record partition or key is specified, or partitioner.ignore.keys is set to true), and if the client rack is specified and there are partition leaders in the same rack, it will select the next partition from those "nearby" partitions. The current algorithm is followed in other aspects, including load balancing.

### Motivation

There are many use cases where it's acceptable from a business logic point of view for a produced record to be appended to any partition of a multi-partition topic. The current default partitioning algorithm takes advantage of this and periodically rotates target partitions (if the partition and key are not set), also taking into account partition load statistics. The KIP is motivated by a typical cloud Kafka setup: the cloud region has multiple availability zones (AZs), the cluster brokers are uniformly distributed across AZs, partition leaders are distributed across AZs, and clients—particularly producers—are also distributed across AZs. Inter-AZ network traffic is not free (true for many cloud providers) and it's desirable to reduce it.

### Configuration & Compatibility

The new behavior will be controlled by configuration, and the changes will be reflected in the documentation to the partitioner.class config, which explains the algorithm to the user. Migrating to the new version will have no impact on clients, as the default configuration value keeps the old behavior.

## Pull Requests

There appear to be two relevant PRs:

1. **The main implementation PR (#19850):** In a discussion thread, Ivan Yurchenko referenced the pull request at https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/19850. An interesting design point raised in the discussion: unlike KIP-392 where the `client.rack` config serves both as setting the rack and as the on/off switch for the whole feature, in KIP-1123 these are separate—the author originally thought having separate configs would be more explicit and more future-proof, in case some other new feature relying on the `client.rack` setting is added.

2. **A Javadoc PR (#22432):** KAFKA-19193: "add Javadoc for rack-aware params in BuiltInPartitioner" — PR #22432, opened May 31, 2026 by ivanyu (Contributor), tagged as a small clients/producer PR.

## Technical Context

The affected class, BuiltInPartitioner, is a core part of the producer's partitioning logic. It's the built-in default partitioner—a utility class used directly from RecordAccumulator that does not implement the Partitioner interface. It keeps track of various bookkeeping information required for adaptive sticky partitioning (described in detail in KIP-794), with one partitioner object per topic.
